title: PRD_HEADER -- the machine-readable identity block at the top of a step-4 PRD
description: ONE fenced ```json block, first in the file, on every step-4 project PRD. It is what makes a PRD machine-readable WITHOUT moving it to a dedicated folder (Andrew memo 2026-09-02: 'a dedicated format that is machine-readable, that COO has a monitor on'; CTO design R3 @3814be3317 chose the header over a folder so no existing citation breaks). CONSUMERS: (1) the R3 commit-trigger monitor reads it to deliver exact PRD identity + version + commit SHA to 2.0.0_SA_COO (CVO~A @0d272d257c: defined and validated BEFORE any monitor is built); (2) the step-6 TO gate's step-4 conformance limb (Andrew-direct 2026-09-02 /open-calls CALL 2, 'All recs approved' -- ONE limb on the EXISTING gate, never a second gate) refuses a TO whose PRD lacks this block, the ENDPOINT section, or the surface manifest; (3) SINCE 2026-09-09 the SURFACE-MANIFEST requirement ALSO refuses AT COMMIT TIME, against the PRD itself -- .tools/prd-manifest-gate.py, wired into .tools/safe-commit.sh, Andrew-direct at the 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z terminal VERBATIM: 'the surface_manifest first of all is mandatory; a PRD literally cannot be committed unless it has one.' HISTORY, because the clause it replaces was load-bearing and its failure is the reason for the change: this description previously read 'A PRD with no header is not refused by itself -- a TO cut against it is', which was TRUE and was the defect -- the refusal pointed at the COO's task order for the CTO's omission, one step too late. NFRA_REPORT's PRD committed clean with no manifest at @ff9900b0ea and the gap was found by Andrew and independently by 2.0.0_SA_COO~ZZ, i.e. by two READERS rather than by the machinery. The commit gate is a CALLER of consumer (2)'s detector (_top_section + MANIFEST_HEADING_RE), never a second copy, so the two cannot drift; its DOMAIN is step==4 only (205 tracked *_PRD.md, 8 are step-4 PRDs) and its blast radius was censused BEFORE it shipped: 0 of 8 refused, hence no legacy carve-out and no audited override. The header-block and ENDPOINT limbs are UNCHANGED and still refuse only at L6. (4) SINCE 2026-09-10 ~21:2xZ (spine v3.14, L4-R, Andrew-direct "CRO and CVO should have to sign off on PRD before COO gets it"): `prd_version` is the KEY the two reviewers' sign-off files bind to -- .tools/prd-header-notify.py withholds the COO delivery until prd/signoff/4.0.0_SA_CRO.json and prd/signoff/3.0.0_SA_CVO.json both read SIGNED at this exact version, and .tools/to-pipeline-gate.py LIMB 6 refuses a task order otherwise; a bump re-opens both. The header itself is unchanged: a sign-off is a file in lane TREE_PRD_SIGNOFF, never a field the author edits.

project.description: Register project code. MUST match org/projects/<project>.json; the gate cross-checks.

directive.description: Directive code. MUST match the register row's `directive` and the DIRECTIVES.yaml member list -- two carriers, compared.

fabric.description: Same enum as the register row and to-pipeline-gate.py:72 FABRIC_ENUM. MUST match the register row.

prd_version.description: Bumped on any substantive edit. The R3 monitor emits on new-or-bumped, so an un-bumped substantive edit is INVISIBLE to COO -- that is the author's obligation and this field is where it is discharged.

step.description: Always 4. Present so a consumer can reject a document that merely LOOKS like a PRD.

brief_ref.description: The L1 ARTIFACT this PRD was written from, WITH its vintage (`<path>@<commit>`). THREE shapes (the tree home `org/missions/D<n>/<MACRO>/<CODE>/brief/<slug>.md` added 2026-09-03 with the canonical workflow v2.0 -- PROJECT_TREE.contract.json names `brief/` as a project subfolder and the header pattern must admit what the contract declares; the two earlier shapes stay). TWO shapes originally, and the domain is declared because the first cut admitted only one (MECE gap found by 3.0.0_SA_CVO 2026-09-02 when limb 5 refused NFRA_COMPEFFICACY's header): (a) a CRO brief, `docs/briefs/<file>@<commit>`; (b) an ANDREW-DIRECT RECORD, `org/tier{n}_{tier}/<serial>/deliverables/ANDREW_DIRECT_<...>.md@<commit>` -- the canonical durable carrier org/XXX.md prescribes for a project he directs at a terminal (three such projects on 2026-09-02 alone). Either way the vintage is REQUIRED: a citation without one is not a citation. Uncovered-member hunt: a project with NO step-1 artifact at all is not a step-4 PRD and is refused by omission, which is the intent. HARDENED 2026-09-02 (CVO~A @dddd96477d falsifier 3): the first pattern used [^@]+ for the filename, which admits '/' and therefore `docs/briefs/../architecture/x.md@...` and `ANDREW_DIRECT_x/../../OTHER.md@...` -- dot-traversal and cross-segment matches. Now: no path segment may be `.` or `..` (negative lookahead), the ANDREW_DIRECT filename is a single segment, and a docs/briefs path is one or more dot-free segments. Referent EXISTENCE is deliberately NOT checked here -- that would be a separately authorized refusal.

endpoint_outcomes.description: Every FWD-n the PRD's ENDPOINT section names. Retired outcomes are NOT listed (their numbers stay vacant). The gate checks each listed id appears in the ENDPOINT section and vice versa.

status.description: DRAFT = written, not yet decomposable. RATIFIED = step 5 may begin. SUPERSEDED = a later prd_version or a different PRD replaced it; cite the successor in the body.
